choices.C: Correlation requires all points to coincide
choices.D: A functional relationship cannot be plotted in a coordinate system

question: What is the difference between statistical correlation and a functional relationship?
solution: A functional relationship assigns exactly one \(y\) to each allowed \(x\). Correlation describes an overall association and need not determine \(y\) exactly. In the linear case illustrated by B, points may scatter around a straight line. Association can also be nonlinear, and correlation can coexist with a function: \(y=x\), with varying \(x\), is an exact function with perfect positive linear correlation. Thus B is the best listed answer, with its straight-line description understood as the linear case.
